policy_title: Increase permanent exclusions and double Pupil Referral Units
stated: Reform UK will implement permanent exclusions for violent and disruptive students and double the number of Pupil Referral Units (PRUs) to ensure schools can function safely and spread best practice.

source.quote: Permanent Exclusions for Violent and Disruptive Students We will double the number of Pupil Referral Units (PRUs) so schools can function safely. We will also ensure that best practice is spread across PRUs.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly affects school standards (removing disruptive students) and the attainment/opportunity of excluded pupils routed to PRUs, whose outcomes are well below mainstream — a non-negligible two-sided educational effect.

The policy is explicitly designed to reduce violence and disruption in schools; the safety consequences for remaining pupils and staff, and the potential displacement of excluded students into communities, earn a real verdict on antisocial behaviour and safety.

UK government data consistently show permanent exclusions fall disproportionately on Black pupils and students with SEND, meaning a policy that increases exclusion rates has a direct and documented equal-treatment dimension for those minority groups.

membership_note: Three fundamentals earn genuine verdicts: O7 is the policy's core educational target; O5 captures both the intended school-safety gain and the displacement risk for excluded students; O9 reflects the well-documented differential impact on minority and SEND pupils, which is a concrete equal-treatment concern, not an incidental one.
